name: Pricing models
description: Per unit, tiered, volume, package and more, with a live calculator.
takeaways: One active pricing model per product
Tiered prices each bracket; volume reprices all units

learn.intro: Every product in Zenskar has exactly one active pricing model. The model decides how a quantity (usually a billable metric) turns into money.

cards.title: Tiered
cards.body: Unit price changes across brackets. Each bracket is priced separately and the bill adds them up.

cards.title: Volume
cards.body: One per-unit price applies to the entire quantity, chosen by the bracket it lands in.
cards.example: Same tiers. 250 units lands in the top tier, so 250 × $80 = $20,000.

cards.title: Package
cards.body: Fixed-size bundles. Partial packages round up.
cards.example: Packages of 50 units at $4,500. A customer using 101 units is billed 3 packages = $13,500.

cards.title: With flat fee
cards.body: Tiered or volume plus a fixed fee per bracket.
cards.example: Volume with flat fee: the top tier has a $250 flat fee. 250 units: $250 + 250 × $80 = $20,250.

cards.title: Step
cards.body: A flat fee per tier, stepping up as usage crosses each threshold.
cards.example: Illustrative fees of $1,000 / $1,500 / $2,000 for tiers 1 / 2 / 3. Usage of 150 lands in tier 2, so the charge is $1,500.

cards.title: Matrix
cards.body: Price depends on two dimensions, such as volume and region.
cards.example: Price per order by restaurant type and region: US/Standard $2.00, US/Premium $3.00, EU/Standard $2.50. An EU Standard order bills $2.50.

cards.title: Percent
cards.body: A percentage of a transaction value or metered amount.

learn.outro: Metered or not? A metered product reads its quantity from a billable metric for the billing period (example: a metric shows 12,400 API calls this month, and the pricing model prices those 12,400). A non-metered product uses a fixed quantity you enter (example: 25 seats).

edgeCases: Boundaries. Exactly 100 units is in tier 1; 101 is in tier 2. Try both in the calculator under tiered and volume: volume jumps down at 101 (100×$100 = $10,000 vs 101×$90 = $9,090).
Zero usage. Per-unit, tiered and volume bill $0. With flat-fee models, check whether the first tier's flat fee still applies when usage is zero.
Open-ended last tier. The top tier has no upper limit. Make sure the tier above your largest expected customer exists.
Partial packages. 1 unit and 50 units both bill one package; 51 bills two.
Flat fee vs usage. In tiered with flat fee, every tier the customer reaches adds its own flat fee, so a customer who barely enters tier 2 still pays tier 2's flat fee.

quiz.question: A customer uses 250 licenses. Tiers: 1–100 at $100, 101–200 at $90, 201+ at $80. What does tiered pricing bill?
Same usage and tiers, but volume pricing. What is the bill?
quiz.explanation: 250 lands in the top tier, so all 250 units cost $80: $20,000.

quiz.question: A package is 50 units and the customer uses 101. How many packages are billed?
quiz.explanation: Partial packages always round up to the next full package.

quiz.question: "The bulk-discount rate should apply to every unit once the customer crosses a threshold." Which model?
quiz.explanation: Volume applies one per-unit price to the entire quantity.

quiz.question: Matrix pricing differs from tiered pricing because it depends on…
options: Two dimensions, such as volume and region
quiz.explanation: Matrix pricing is multi-dimensional; tiered is 1-dimensional.

qa.question: Tiered vs volume: what is the difference?
qa.answer: Tiered prices each bracket separately and adds them up. Volume finds the bracket the total quantity lands in and prices every unit at that rate. With $100/$90/$80 brackets and 250 units: tiered $23,000, volume $20,000.

qa.question: Volume vs package?
qa.answer: Volume changes the per-unit price by quantity. Package sells fixed-size bundles at a fixed price each and rounds partial bundles up.

qa.question: Tiered vs tiered with flat fee?
qa.answer: The flat-fee variant adds a fixed fee for each bracket the usage reaches, on top of the per-unit rate inside that bracket.

qa.question: Volume vs volume with flat fee?
qa.answer: Plain volume is quantity × the bracket rate. With a flat fee, the bracket's flat fee is added once.

qa.question: Step vs tiered?
qa.answer: Per the docs summary, step charges a flat fee per tier as usage crosses each threshold; tiered charges per unit inside each bracket. Confirm exact step behaviour with an SME.

qa.question: Matrix vs tiered?
qa.answer: Tiered looks at one quantity. Matrix looks up a price using two dimensions, such as region and plan.

qa.question: Per unit vs percent?
qa.answer: Per unit multiplies a count by a price. Percent applies a rate to an amount, such as 2.5% of payments processed.

qa.question: Metered vs non-metered product?
qa.answer: A metered product reads its quantity from a billable metric for the billing period. A non-metered product uses a fixed quantity you enter, such as 25 seats.

qa.question: Point-in-time vs period-of-time product?
qa.answer: Point-in-time products are charged for events as they occur. Period-of-time products are charged for a span, like a subscription. In the V3 docs, point-in-time allows quantity or credits subtypes; period-of-time allows quantity or feature.

qa.question: Product vs pricing?
qa.answer: The product is what you sell. Pricing (a pricing preset or model) is how it is priced. A product can have pricing presets attached.

qa.question: A seat license with a bulk discount for every seat?
qa.answer: Volume pricing: once the customer crosses the threshold, all seats get the lower rate.

qa.question: API calls with a cheaper rate for higher usage bands?
qa.answer: Tiered pricing: early calls keep their price and only calls inside a band get that band's rate.

qa.question: Selling credits in blocks of 1,000?
qa.answer: Package pricing: each block of 1,000 is one billable package, and partial blocks round up.

qa.question: Charging a payment processing fee as a share of volume?
qa.answer: Percent pricing.

qa.question: Price depends on restaurant tier and region?
qa.answer: Matrix pricing. The metric returns a quantity plus dimension columns, and the matrix looks up a price per combination.

qa.question: A platform fee plus usage?
qa.answer: Either tiered or volume with flat fee, or two products on the contract: a fixed subscription and a metered one.

qa.question: What changes between exactly 100 and 101 units under volume pricing?
qa.answer: With brackets 1–100 at $100 and 101–200 at $90: 100 units cost $10,000 but 101 units cost $9,090, so the bill goes down.

qa.question: What does zero usage bill?
qa.answer: Per unit, tiered and volume bill $0. For flat-fee models check whether the first bracket's flat fee applies.

qa.question: Can a product's type change after pricing exists?
qa.answer: No. The V3 docs block a type change once pricing presets exist (PRODUCT_TYPE_CHANGE_WITH_PRICING).

qa.question: Can I delete or deactivate a product used in contracts?
qa.answer: Deleting is blocked while any contract references it. Setting it inactive is blocked if an active contract uses it.

qa.question: Can I edit pricing on an already created product?
qa.answer: The V3 docs list editing pricing on an existing product as not yet available. Check your tenant.

qa.question: Can two products share a SKU?
qa.answer: No. SKU must be unique in the organization (PRODUCT_SKU_DUPLICATE). Product name uniqueness is currently not enforced.

qa.question: How does a metered product get its quantity?
qa.answer: A billable metric filters rows, matches the customer, keeps the period and aggregates. The result is the quantity the pricing model prices.

qa.question: What are dimensions?
qa.answer: Columns returned by a SQL metric alongside the quantity column. Dimensional pricing, such as matrix, uses them.

qa.question: What does archived mean for a product?
qa.answer: End of life. It is unavailable for new usage and cannot be set when creating a product.
